title: Four-Week Sprint
summary: An intensive 28-day plan for students with a test date about a month away and a baseline score: diagnose fast, fix the highest-yield domains, rehearse the harder modules, then taper with the final-14-days protocol. About 12–13 hours a week for three weeks, lighter in the final week.

resources.label: SAT Practice Bank (filter by domain, skill and difficulty)

error_codes.meaning: Content: did not know the rule, formula or skill
Process: knew it but set it up or read it wrongly
Time: rushed or ran out of time
Named slip: a specific, nameable careless error
Guess-right: correct but unsure; review as a miss

schedule.who_for: You already know the test format, have a full-test baseline (or will take one on day 1), and have a test date roughly four weeks away. Not suitable for building foundations from scratch; use the Twelve-Week Foundation plan for that.
rules: Every miss and every guess goes into the Notebook with a cause code and rule sentence on the same day.
Fix targets come from mock data, not from feelings: the two highest (misses × official domain weight).
No new topics in the last 48 hours before the test.
Sunday is rest unless a mock is scheduled.

phases.label: Diagnose and high-yield fixes
phases.goal: Baseline mock, cause-coded review, and fast fixes in rule-based domains (conventions, linear algebra).

phases.label: Targeted repair
phases.goal: Two-domain repair driven by the mock, plus a second full mock to confirm.

phases.label: Hard-module rehearsal
phases.goal: Hard-only drills on trap families and timed modules; begin the final-14-days schedule.

phases.label: Taper and test
phases.goal: Final full test, rule sheet, logistics, rest, test day.

weeks.label: Week 1: Diagnose and high-yield fixes

tasks: Full timed mock in the SAT simulator (https://sat.schood.online) at your real test time; one sitting with a 10-minute break
After the mock: 15-minute note on energy, timing and the hardest questions; no review yet
Forensic review of the mock: re-solve each missed, guessed and slow question before reading the explanation; assign cause codes C/P/T/X/G; name the trap; write a rule sentence
Log misses and guesses in the Notebook with a cause code and a rule sentence (https://practice.sat.schood.online/notebook)
Count misses by domain; multiply by official weight; pick the two fix targets for weeks 1–2
Read R&W: Standard English Conventions — boundaries (/reading-writing-conventions), 25 min
SAT Practice Bank: 25 medium questions in Standard English Conventions → Boundaries (https://practice.sat.schood.online/bank); review every miss
Clear due Reviews (https://practice.sat.schood.online/reviews), 10 min
Read Math: Algebra — systems and linear functions (/math-algebra), 25 min
SAT Practice Bank: 25 medium questions in Algebra → Systems of linear equations and Linear functions (https://practice.sat.schood.online/bank); review every miss
Read Desmos and Calculator Strategy — graphing both sides (/desmos-and-calculator-strategy), 15 min
SAT Practice Bank: 20 medium questions in Standard English Conventions → Form, structure and sense (https://practice.sat.schood.online/bank); review every miss
SAT Practice Bank: 15 medium questions in Algebra → Linear inequalities (https://practice.sat.schood.online/bank); review every miss
Re-solve Notebook entries from the last 2–3 days without notes; close only correct re-solves
Timed R&W module set: 27 mixed R&W questions in 32 minutes from the SAT Practice Bank, timer on
Timed Math module set: 22 mixed Math questions in 35 minutes from the SAT Practice Bank, timer on, Desmos allowed
Compare target-domain misses with the baseline mock
Rest day: no SAT work. Optional 20 minutes of reading nonfiction you enjoy

weeks.checkpoint: Pass: conventions and linear-algebra misses in the timed sets are clearly fewer than in the baseline mock. If not: repeat the week 1 drills on days 1–2 of week 2 before moving on.

weeks.label: Week 2: Targeted repair

tasks: Read R&W: Information and Ideas — command of evidence (/reading-writing-information-ideas), 25 min
SAT Practice Bank: 20 medium and hard questions in Information and Ideas → Command of evidence (textual and quantitative) (https://practice.sat.schood.online/bank); review every miss
Clear due Reviews (https://practice.sat.schood.online/reviews), 10 min
Read Math: Advanced Math — quadratics and the discriminant (/math-advanced-math), 25 min
SAT Practice Bank: 20 medium and hard questions in Advanced Math → Nonlinear equations and systems (https://practice.sat.schood.online/bank); review every miss
Log misses and guesses in the Notebook with a cause code and a rule sentence (https://practice.sat.schood.online/notebook)
SAT Practice Bank: 20 medium and hard questions in Expression of Ideas → Rhetorical synthesis and Transitions (https://practice.sat.schood.online/bank); review every miss
SAT Practice Bank: 15 medium questions in Advanced Math → Nonlinear functions (exponential models) (https://practice.sat.schood.online/bank); review every miss
Read Desmos Power Moves (premium) — Moves 1–4 (/guide-desmos-power-moves), 30 min
SAT Practice Bank: 15 hard questions in Algebra and Advanced Math, solved with sliders or graphs where faster (https://practice.sat.schood.online/bank); review every miss
Re-solve Notebook entries from the last 2–3 days without notes; close only correct re-solves
Clear due Reviews (https://practice.sat.schood.online/reviews), 15 min
Light day before the mock: 10 easy questions per section; pack the mock as if it were test day
Full official Bluebook practice test (one you have not taken) at your real test time; one sitting with a 10-minute break
Forensic review of the mock: re-solve each missed, guessed and slow question before reading the explanation; assign cause codes C/P/T/X/G; name the trap; write a rule sentence
Log misses and guesses in the Notebook with a cause code and a rule sentence (https://practice.sat.schood.online/notebook)
Compare with mock 1: codes that repeat are the targets for week 3

weeks.checkpoint: Pass: mock 2 shows fewer misses in the week 1–2 target domains than mock 1, and fewer P/X codes. If a target domain did not improve, keep it as a target in week 3 and change the method (slower untimed sets, then timed).

weeks.label: Week 3: Hard-module rehearsal
focus: Trap families from the hard-module guides

tasks: Read R&W Hard-Module Traps (premium) — trap families matching your repeated codes (/guide-rw-hard-module-traps), 30 min
SAT Practice Bank: 20 hard questions in your weakest R&W skill from mock 2 (https://practice.sat.schood.online/bank); review every miss
Clear due Reviews (https://practice.sat.schood.online/reviews), 10 min
Read Math Hard-Module Traps (premium) — trap families matching your repeated codes (/guide-math-hard-module-traps), 30 min
SAT Practice Bank: 20 hard questions in your weakest Math skill from mock 2 (https://practice.sat.schood.online/bank); review every miss
Timed R&W module set: 27 mixed R&W questions in 32 minutes from the SAT Practice Bank, timer on
Timed Math module set: 22 mixed Math questions in 35 minutes from the SAT Practice Bank, timer on, Desmos allowed
Count misses only in the two targets; log slow questions as well as wrong ones
SAT Practice Bank: 15 hard questions in mixed R&W (interleaved skills) (https://practice.sat.schood.online/bank); review every miss
SAT Practice Bank: 12 hard questions in mixed Math (interleaved skills) (https://practice.sat.schood.online/bank); review every miss
Re-solve Notebook entries from weeks 2–3 without notes; close only correct re-solves
Read The Final 14 Days (premium) — the forensic review protocol and logistics (/guide-final-14-days), 20 min
Logistics check: device requirements, Bluebook updated, photo ID, calculator batteries, route
Clear due Reviews (https://practice.sat.schood.online/reviews), 15 min
Full timed mock in the SAT simulator (https://sat.schood.online) at your real test time; one sitting with a 10-minute break (final-14-days test 2)
Forensic review of the mock: re-solve each missed, guessed and slow question before reading the explanation; assign cause codes C/P/T/X/G; name the trap; write a rule sentence
Write the first draft of your ten-rule sheet

weeks.checkpoint: Pass: three mocks show a stable or rising trend, and no trap family appears in all three. If one does, give it the whole of day 1 in week 4.

weeks.label: Week 4: Taper and test

tasks: Full official Bluebook practice test (one you have not taken) at your real test time; one sitting with a 10-minute break (final full test, dress rehearsal)
Forensic review of the mock: re-solve each missed, guessed and slow question before reading the explanation; assign cause codes C/P/T/X/G; name the trap; write a rule sentence
Finalise the ten-rule sheet by hand
Exam setup in Bluebook and admission ticket (available 5 days before the test): complete setup, print the ticket, email it to yourself
Timed R&W module set: 27 mixed R&W questions in 32 minutes from the SAT Practice Bank, timer on
Read your rule sheet
Re-solve Notebook entries from the last 10 days without notes; close only correct re-solves
Timed Math module set: 22 mixed Math questions in 35 minutes from the SAT Practice Bank, timer on, Desmos allowed
Read your rule sheet
Rules and Desmos refresh: 15 conventions questions; rehearse your five most-used Desmos moves once each
Confirm route and arrival time from your admission ticket
Warm-up only: 6 easy R&W and 6 easy Math questions
Pack your bag with the checklist in The Final 14 Days (/guide-final-14-days); charge the device
Test eve or test day: follow the test-eve and test-day routines in The Final 14 Days. If your test is later in the week, shift days 1–6 so that day 6 is the eve

weeks.checkpoint: Pass: you arrive at the test with the device charged, exam setup completed, ticket and physical ID, and no new material studied in the last 48 hours.

checkpoints.title: Baseline and targets
checkpoints.pass_rule: Two fix targets chosen from weighted mock data; Notebook started.
checkpoints.if_not: Do not start week 2 drills until targets are chosen.

checkpoints.title: Mock 2 comparison
checkpoints.pass_rule: Target-domain misses and P/X codes lower than mock 1.
checkpoints.if_not: Keep the same targets; switch to untimed method-first sets for two days.

checkpoints.title: Trend check
checkpoints.pass_rule: Stable or rising mock trend; no trap family in all three mocks.
checkpoints.if_not: Spend week 4 day 1 on the repeated family instead of a full test only if the test is more than 7 days away.

checkpoints.title: Ready to test
checkpoints.pass_rule: Logistics complete; rule sheet written; rest routine followed.
checkpoints.if_not: Logistics are not optional: finish exam setup and ticket before anything else.
